root_cause.text: The `sev_ioctl_do_pdh_export` function in the AMD CCP driver failed to validate the PSP command return status and firmware error codes before copying certificate data to userspace, allowing firmware-reported lengths to trigger out-of-bounds memory access when the command failed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a check `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free_cert;` immediately before the `copy_to_user` calls in `drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev.c`, preventing execution when the underlying command fails; the CVE description confirms that copying bytes based on firmware requirements without checking command success causes slab-out-of-bounds reads.

intent_record.what: Replaced a single-line comment with a multi-line comment explaining that firmware returns blob lengths (minimum or actual) which are then passed to the user.
intent_record.how: No functional impact on runtime behavior; solely improves code documentation clarity regarding the data flow between firmware and user space.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add validation for error states before PDH blob processing to ensure correct cleanup and prevent invalid execution.
intent_record.what: Inserted a conditional check evaluating 'ret' or 'argp->error' before processing the pdh_blob, directing execution to the 'e_free_cert' cleanup label if either condition is true.
intent_record.how: Prevents the function from proceeding with data copying or further operations when previous steps failed or an error flag was set, ensuring proper resource cleanup and error propagation.
